entries.root_cause: Authenticating commit-status evidence only by the shared github-actions[bot] creator and by pointing at a successful canonical workflow run was insufficient: any repository workflow with status-write authority can publish under the same bot identity and can point a forged status at a legitimate run for a different PR, command mode, or coordinate set. The status therefore was not yet bound to the actual trusted publisher job that produced it.

The live readiness verifier revalidated current head/base SHAs and mutable labels but treated any non-empty current head ref as acceptable. A branch rename can preserve the exact candidate commit while invalidating the canonical G1 branch-prefix classification, so SHA-only readiness left non-SHA implementation identity mutable after attestation.

The issue_comment workflow initially accepted github.event.repository.default_branch as the authoritative branch name. That event field is a creation-time snapshot, so a repository default-branch change during execution could leave resolve, final publication, and later readiness validating against a branch that was no longer the repository's current default branch.
